Claim: PM loop round 9 — flight C2a, maintainer-directed (「同意你的建议，你负责执行派发所有可行的优化」, 2026-09-07): the scheduled shard-timings refresh workflow, with #16473 folded in as its prerequisite — flight C1 (#16173) measured at 03:2xZ that the artifact host (`productionresultssa*.blob.core.windows.net`) is denied to every agent container by egress policy, so the documented refresh cannot run from a dev worktree; the refresh therefore runs IN-RUNNER, where `.turbo/runs/*.json` already sits, and this workflow's first `workflow_dispatch` is the refresh itself — the PR it opens is #16173's deliverable. Rider #16473: `buildDataset` in `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` bypasses its median rule for a file-sharded package (last run wins; slices from different runs summed into a weight no run measured) — fixed first, with self-test cases, so the refresh's `@objectstack/cli` weight is a median like every other package's.
Session: `session_019RfFHiRCSs3JXLK4cwcfox`
Branch: `claude/issue-16464-shard-timings-refresh-workflow`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-16464`
Domain: `domain:devx` (dispatched by the skills seat on the maintainer's direction)
File surface: `.github/workflows/shard-timings-refresh.yml` (new), `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs` (the slice ledger's merge rule + self-test), one helper under `scripts/ci/` if the pin update needs one; `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` is written only by the workflow run, never by hand. ⛔ `ci.yml` untouched; no `timeout-minutes`, matrix or bound change.
Container & model: S, `mode:subagent`, opus — `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier`: no path-derived mandate.
Clause-②: no
Serial: no open PR touches the measure script or the JSON (C1 produced no PR); flights V and X hold `ci.yml`, which this card does not touch. Not governed ⇒ in-seat review, then the seat flips ready and arms SQUASH auto-merge; `skip-changeset`. The PR carries `Fixes #16464` and `Fixes #16473`; #16173 and #16222 are `Refs` (they close when the workflow's first refresh PR merges).

Implemented as the prerequisite rider of flight C2a, on branch `claude/issue-16464-shard-timings-refresh-workflow`. Draft PR: https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/16498 (it carries the closing keyword for this card). The full `os-dev-report` for both cards is https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/16464#issuecomment-5565145010; this is the pointer, so the fix is discoverable from the card that describes it.

**Shape taken: A, with B folded in as the guard that makes A's default safe.** The card offered three. A alone (key the ledger per input group) leaves the ungrouped call resolving multiple runs by last-wins exactly as before; B alone (refuse any repeat) makes a multi-run refresh of a sliced package impossible, which the card names as its cost. Together they compose without either cost: slices are summed **within** a run, the per-run sums are medianed **across** runs, and a repeat within one declared group — which can only mean two runs sharing a group — is a named refusal with `--run` given as the remedy. C was not taken: it documents the defect rather than removing it, and the dataset it would annotate is machine-generated input to a scheduling decision, not something a human reads before each split.

The grouping key comes from the caller, as the card's shape A anticipated, because a run summary carries no run identifier to infer one from. `--run` opens a group; summaries before any `--run` share one implicit group, which is the ordinary single-run refresh the scheduled workflow performs.

**Measured, red then green.** The red leg reproduces flight C1's scratch driver of the exported `buildDataset`, and the numbers are the card's own:

```text
                                       BEFORE   AFTER   correct
three runs measuring 400/600/1000s      1000      600     600
unsliced control (100/300/500)            300      300     300
run B 1/2 + B 2/2 + run C 1/2             800      600     600
  skippedIncompleteSlices                  []   named      named
```

The `AFTER` splice row reads `cli in run C (missing 2/2)` — the partial set is attributed to the run that could not assemble it, rather than silently completed from another run's slice.

Also corrected: `provenance.mergeRule` said `median across summaries`, which was only ever true of unsliced packages, since a sliced package's summaries are PARTS of one measurement rather than repeats of it. It now states both composed rules, and `provenance.runs` records the declared ids.

Seven self-test cases, battery floor 34 to 41, and the whole path exercised through the real CLI on synthetic summaries as well as through `buildDataset` directly.

Load-bearing for #16464 rather than incidental: the refresh workflow feeds one run today, but the moment anyone feeds more than one — which the #16173 refresh recipe explicitly directs — the heaviest package in the workspace would have taken a single observation while every other package took a median, with no line of output saying so.

Pointer correction: the report link in my comment above now points at a superseded report. The current one is https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/16464#issuecomment-5567426497 (status `needs_decision`).

⚠️ The change of status is about the WORKFLOW card only, and nothing about this card moved. This rider is fully repaired, self-tested and proven live, and PR #16498 still binds its closing keyword to this card alone. If anything, the live runs strengthened it: the workflow now has to feed SEVEN runs to the generator to cover the workspace, so the per-run assembly this card added is not a hygiene fix on a path nobody walks — it is the only reason that path is correct. Across those seven runs the generator raised no ambiguity refusal, which is the behaviour this card specified.

Final pointer: the current report is https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/16464#issuecomment-5567897750 (status `done`), superseding the two before it. PR #16498 binds this card's closing keyword and is green on head `94eeaa19b1`.

Nothing about this card changed across the three reports — it was repaired, self-tested and proven live in the first round. What changed is how load-bearing it turned out to be: the refresh lane was ruled to merge rather than replace, so it now feeds the generator several runs' summaries under per-run `--run` groups as a matter of course, and the live green run did exactly that with no ambiguity refusal. The per-run assembly this card added is not hygiene on a path nobody walks; it is the reason that path is correct.
